title: CI Performance Gate: Automated P95 and tokens/sec Regression Detection
creator: Ava Chen
description: Add a CI gating job that runs a lightweight but statistically-sound performance harness on every PR touching the runtime or model adapters. The job will compare PR results against a stored baseline and fail the PR if an actionable regression is detected on primary metrics (tokens/sec and p95 latency). The goal is to catch regressions early without adding >5 minutes to the median PR feedback loop.
acceptance_criteria:
1) CI job (perf-gate/pr) runs on PRs that touch modules listed in docs and returns pass/fail with summary metrics.
2) Baseline artifacts stored per-branch+commit tag in S3 with metadata (seed, model, tokenizer, compiler flags).
3) Regression detection uses both relative and absolute thresholds plus a simple bootstrap-based significance check to avoid flaky gating.
4) Dashboard link to recent PR runs visible in Console and in GitHub PR checks.
5) Run time of the job is typically under 8 minutes for warmup+measure on the CI runner fleet.
6) Documentation and runbook created for investigating failing perf gates.
approach_summary:
- Single-test harness that executes 50 short inferences across 3 sequence lengths (32, 128, 512) using a deterministic prompt set.
- Warmup phase: 10 iterations to populate KV cache when applicable.
- Measure tokens/sec (aggregate over measured iterations) and p95 latency per sequence length.
- Compare to baseline using: relative threshold (default 5% regression), absolute floor for noisy metrics (tokens/sec > 20 tps), and a simple non-parametric bootstrap for p95 difference to control false positives.
- Fail gating when both relative threshold and bootstrap indicate regression, or when absolute difference exceeds emergency limits.
- Persist raw samples + summary JSON to S3 and annotate PR with the summary and link to detailed artifacts.
test_plan:
1) Implement harness as a small Python script in tools/perf_gate/ that can run local and in CI.
2) Add GitHub Actions workflow perf-gate-pr.yaml that triggers on pull_request for paths under /runtime/, /model_adapters/, /compilers/.
3) Provide a switch to run 'smoke' vs 'full' mode. CI uses smoke (50 samples), maintainers can trigger full (500 samples) manually.
4) Add baseline generation job that runs nightly on main and writes baselines to s3://redwood-perf-baselines/runtime-1.21/.
5) Integrate metric upload to Grafana/Prometheus for trend analysis and include an embeddable dashboard in PR status checks.
6) Create runbook for triage: how to reproduce locally, known noisy patterns, and rollback guidance.
notes:
2026-03-10: Initial spike and PoC harness implemented (tools/perf_gate/) using local Docker runner. Sample harness produces tokens/sec and p95 samples; observed ~3.6% run-to-run variance on CI hardware.
2026-03-11: Reworked sampling to include warmup and fixed RNG seed for prompts; variance down to ~1.8% for tokens/sec on stable images.
2026-03-12: Implemented bootstrap test (1000 resamples) for p95 comparison; found that small sample sizes understate tails so combined p95 check with an absolute latency floor.
2026-03-13: Integrated artifact upload to S3 and added annotation script to post summary back to PR. Opened GH PR #1289 to add GitHub Actions workflow.
2026-03-14: Design review with PM/Observability: Diego requested addition of a secondary metric (90th percentile) and a configurable per-model threshold map. Marked for in-review and requested security review for S3 access pattern (ticket created ENG-4830).
implementation_notes:
- Use the same model binary and compiler flags as CI runtime images to avoid skew.
- For Dedicated customers, allow opt-out via a repo-level config file (perf-gate.yaml).
- Avoid running full dataset; prefer synthetic but representative prompts captured from anonymized production telemetry (stored in secure bucket).
- Keep job permissions minimal: CI runner role only needs PutObject to specific baseline prefix and GetObject to compare.
- Track run metadata: runner type, kernel version, model checkpoint hash, quantization profile.
next_steps:
1) Merge GH PR that adds perf-gate workflow and the harness (owner: Diego).
2) Run 7-day nightly baseline generation and validate stability across runners.
3) Add per-model threshold config and wire into gating logic.
4) Add a lightweight Slack alerting hook for unexpected increases in CI gate failure rate.

postmortem_plan: If a false positive gate blocks release, run a manual rerun with full-mode on a pinned runner and compare to nightly baseline; if discrepancy is due to CI runner variance, mark the PR as a flaky-perf-check and adjust thresholds or runner selectors. Record the incident in the runtime postmortem board with timeline and corrective actions.
notes_public: This ticket implements the first stage of continuous performance regression detection in CI: fast, repeatable, and low-false-positive gating for p95 and tokens/sec. It is intentionally conservative to avoid disrupting developer flow while surfacing real regressions early.
